issue_request: FHIR-17357 was Published/Persuasive for STU3. It asked FHIR-core datatypes to make clear that canonical references may include hashtag/fragment references, especially where a reference identifies an ElementDefinition inside a StructureDefinition, with an absent fragment referring to the root element.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 13945. Git commit 8e46cfb7a23bb6b6839535087993eb18253bf523, titled "GF#17357 - explain fragments on canonicals", added fragment-reference wording to source/datatypes.html; later FHIR-18673 wording refinements preserved that allowance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps datatypes and Questionnaire in current build scope. The current canonical datatype text permits #fragment references and says canonical URLs are absolute URIs or fragment identifiers. Questionnaire.item.definition is currently uri, not canonical, after later Questionnaire evolution including FHIR-23765, but its source explicitly documents StructureDefinition canonical URL plus Element.id fragment and root-element behavior. No active source declares a canonical targetProfile of ElementDefinition.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already preserves the implementer-facing rule requested by FHIR-17357, and adding a new generic canonical(ElementDefinition) rule would be redundant or stale against the current source shape.
